question: How do all-patch slide prediction, selected-patch pseudo-label supervision and relative-attention display use different inputs and conditions?

elements.role: WSI bag, fixed patch features, learned compression/shared attention backbone, class-specific attention and independent slide scoring heads.
Patch-axis attention normalization, class-axis softmax and display percentiles are distinct quantities.
Observed training label Y selects in-class bottom/top B, yielding pseudo0/1. B counts selected patches at each extreme.
Selected patch identities and learned features enter clustering scores; pseudo targets enter auxiliary loss.
Other-class top B receives pseudo0 only under mutually exclusive tissue-class assumption; otherwise skip only that supervision.
Predicted class chooses raw pre-normalization attention; percentile mapping and patch locations form a relative display, not pathology truth.

feature computation distinct from target supervision
